fullPassage: Sarah, a young artist with a love for painting, entered a local art contest. As she looked at the amazing artworks made by others, her confidence dropped. She quietly thought, ‘I might not win an award.’ The moment of judgment arrived, and the judges began announcing winners one by one. It wasn’t until the end that she heard her name. The head of the judges said, “Congratulations, Sarah Parker! You won first prize. We loved the uniqueness of your work.” Sarah was overcome with joy, and she couldn’t stop smiling. This experience meant more than just winning; it confirmed her identity as an artist.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① making → made: artworks made by others = 다른 사람들에 의해 만들어진 작품 (과거분사 수동).
det.analysis:
❌ ① making → made: 작품이 만들어진 것이므로 수동(과거분사 made). making은 능동.
✅ ② that: It wasn't until ~ that = 강조구문, 올바름
✅ ③ overcome: be overcome with = 압도되다, 과거분사 올바름
✅ ④ meant: mean의 과거형, 올바름
det.tip: 능동 vs 수동 분사: artworks made(만들어진) by others / artworks making(만드는) — 작품은 만들어지는 것

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② to smile → smiling: stop + V-ing = ~하는 것을 멈추다. stop + to V = ~하기 위해 멈추다. 여기서는 미소를 멈출 수 없었다는 뜻.
det.analysis:
✅ ① thought: 과거 시제, 올바름
❌ ② to smile → smiling: couldn't stop smiling = 미소를 멈출 수 없었다. stop + V-ing 패턴.
✅ ③ meant: 과거 시제, 올바름
✅ ④ confirmed: 과거 시제, 올바름
det.tip: stop + V-ing(~하는 것을 멈추다) vs stop + to V(~하기 위해 멈추다)
